Ajax is nice and all but it would be awesome to have an option to view all comments at once without needing to click to read more or to click a tiny + sign to read a comment that has been marked as zero. The Slashdot way, which may be of interest, is to not show negative comments by default and to allow a reader to choose to view all comments or not all comments by default. That negates the whole SEO thing as the search engines are never logged in users.

It would be nice to load all comments (or a reasonable threshold of, say, 500 to keep server load down to a dull roar but what good is RAM if you're not using it?) and then, maybe, have an AJAX-y function below a comment that was made while you were reading the thread. It should fail gracefully, of course, for those who do not allow JavaScript to run in the browser. HTML5 may work but I've never learned how to do it so I have no idea if it is possible.

Some of us like to read the comments and actually have conversations with people - without fighting and arguing. It'd be nice to be able to read it all without having to keep clicking constantly or scrolling to the bottom. I know it may not seem like much but it is a viewing/usability feature that I know I am fond of. Maybe you could even make it a new setting where you can select how many new comments are shown with each expansion up to a certain level - if you're worried about compute cycle loads or something. If you run into hardware issues then, maybe, have a special fund drive just to put funds away for new hardware?

Anyhow, just my thoughts. I looked but did not see anything quite like this. It's a trivial annoyance that I am able (and willing) to deal with. I have no idea if I am alone in that matter but I have worked on SMF forums as a developer and mod developer. A number of them indicated that they had high numbers of people who opted to show the larger sizes, with the most replies, as a general rule so I doubt I am alone though this format is different. As it is being loaded fewer times and they are all done at once it may actuallysave on CPU cycles? I am not a DB Wizard though - those guys are weird.

Thoughts? Feedback? Worthwhile solution? Not a pressing matter? Back of the bus? First World Problems? I'm a harbinger of doom? You know, the quality, constructive, feedback normally provided. ;-)

Not only that but it seems like the ajax thing would generate a lot more calls to a db then just loading the comment tree structure right off the bat. I can't see how not loading ~50 more lines of text is saving anything.
